# KnowledgeBot AI — Specification Index

The full specification lives in `KnowledgeBot-AI.md` (3,816 lines). It is split here so agents can load only the sections a task needs. **Every file below is a verbatim extract** — the split adds a title header and nothing else. When spec and code disagree, the spec is authoritative until an ADR says otherwise.

Cite sections as `docs/<file>.md §<n>`.

**Do not edit `01`–`21`.** A deviation is recorded as an ADR, never by rewriting the extract. The one
place the rule is relaxed is `19-repo-structure-adrs.md` **§28**, which is where new ADRs are appended —
§27 and every ADR-001…010 entry there remain verbatim. Writable files in this directory: `00`, `19` §28,
`22`, `23`.

| [19-repo-structure-adrs.md](19-repo-structure-adrs.md) | §27–28 | Monorepo layout and every ADR — `grep -c '^### ADR-' 19-repo-structure-adrs.md` is the count, and the highest number is the last heading in the file; do not restate either here (ADR-036). **Every number is `Accepted`** — ADR-036 was the last `Proposed` one and was accepted 2026-08-12 as option (a), narrowed. Three are **narrow supersessions**: ADR-033 replaces ADR-012's table list, ADR-037 replaces ADR-026's fail-open reasoning, and ADR-060 replaces the `*_visible` rejection inside ADR-056's amendment — in all three the superseded ADR's decision stands and only the named claim moves. That is the whole list; `grep -n '^\*\*Status:.*Supersedes' 19-repo-structure-adrs.md | grep -v 'Supersedes nothing'` re-measures it — anchored to the status line on purpose, because an unanchored `Supersedes` also matches the two ADRs that supersede *spec text* rather than another ADR (016, 030), which is a different thing. ADR-038…043 came from the auth-and-session effort of 2026-08-13 and supersede nothing; ADR-044…046 came from the shutdown-determinism effort of 2026-08-14 — dev never self-restarts, a stop signal must be one PID 1 handles, and the `edge` subnet is pinned outside Docker's dynamic address pool — of which only the last changes an earlier value, and it changes the default rather than the decision; **ADR-047…052** came from the provider-connection and model-catalogue effort of 2026-08-19 and supersede nothing — credential rotation as its own re-authenticating endpoint that is deliberately *permitted* on a revoked or invalid connection, `key_version` as the KEK's version so a rotation bumps a separate `credential_version`, a guarded hard delete that surfaces the embedding designation's `ON DELETE RESTRICT` as an actionable 409, exact pricing columns whose ceiling sits above the FormRequest bound, the capability vocabulary kept out of `packages/contracts`, and a relay that carries the whole error envelope. Two of those six overturned the brief that asked for them, and one — ADR-052 — closes at the relay boundary a property ADR-029 had already decided, without changing it. **ADR-053…054** followed the same day and close `docs/22` § J2 and § J1: an `actionable` boolean on the error envelope saying whether its `message` was written for a person, and a capability flag ruled to be a **claim** that the catalogue write path deliberately does not verify. **ADR-055…059** came from the bots-schema step of 2026-08-19 and supersede nothing — the ordered fallback chain as a table because `jsonb` cannot carry a foreign key (with the snapshot counter-argument recorded and answered), `bots.view` granted to all four roles as an **extension of §6.4/§6.5 rather than a reading of them**, an evidence threshold that is nullable with no default and stored beside its scale because a default would fail no test, `tenantPair()` activated in half with the canary in a bot field until Phase C, and the repo's first paginated list envelope. ADR-058 closes `docs/22` § H9 in part; ADR-056 is the only ADR in the file that adds a capability the specification does not describe, and it says so in its own status line. **ADR-060…061** came from the two Phase B audits and are the two halves of one data-loss finding (`docs/22` § M3): a response that states its own projection, and a client that omits a withheld field from form state rather than seeding it `null`. **ADR-060 is the third narrow supersession here**, after ADR-033 and ADR-037 — it overturns the `*_visible` rejection inside ADR-056's amendment and nothing else in ADR-056 moves, which makes it the register's clearest worked example of a rejected alternative becoming the fix once the reason it was rejected turned out to be false. **ADR-062…065** came from **Phase C, step C1** on 2026-08-20 — the source-cascade migrations — and supersede nothing, but three of the four deviate from verbatim spec (`docs/11` §16.4) and the fourth deviates from an accepted skill: one active-version pointer and no sibling, an `ocr_cfg_version` the spec omits together with `activated_at`/`retired_at` rather than `published_at`, one 15-value status vocabulary on all three tables, and `content_hash` as `char(64)` hex against `postgresql-patterns`' `bytea`. **ADR-065 is not the first ADR to overrule a skill — ADR-047 did, over `kb-security-baseline` §18.4's worked example — but it is the first where the skill correction has *not* landed**, so the register and an accepted skill disagree in writing until it does. That is why the ADR names the obligation instead of discharging it (`docs/22` § P1, open; § J7 is the closed precedent). **ADR-066…068** came from the rest of **Phase C** on 2026-08-21 — the upload transport and intake gate, the lifecycle endpoints and signed callback, bot–source assignment and the deletion path's follow-through — and supersede nothing, but **all three contradict an accepted skill and none of the corrections has landed**: `original/` hoisted out of the version prefix to a sibling of `versions/` because the control plane structurally cannot know a version id at intake (against `seaweedfs-s3` NN1 and `kb-tenancy-isolation`:97), `X-KB-Bot-Id` absent on ingestion because a source is org-owned and bot access is a query-time filter (against `kb-internal-api-contracts`:64), and `docs/08` §13.3 read as the **ingest** key's component list rather than the transport replay key's, which are two different keys with deliberately different components (against the same skill's :122 and :208). The register therefore now carries four open skill divergences — `docs/22` § P1, § Q11, § Q12, § Q13 — against one closed precedent, and `grep -n "^### .*owed by the skill" 22-spec-findings-and-decisions.md` is how to re-measure that rather than trusting this sentence — and, at the foot, **ADR-073…075** from the adapter, RAG-stage and conversation-schema effort of 2026-08-26/27, which supersede nothing and of which two are *applications* of an accepted ADR rather than departures from one: the **BM25 analyzer** (NFKC → casefold → NFKC, character bigrams for unsegmented scripts, word-character runs elsewhere), pinned at `bm25/v1` **only while no corpus has ever been indexed**, which is written as its expiry rather than as a revisit trigger; **`retrieval_traces` off the write allow-list** because ADR-033's property 2 bites the moment an admin screen reads the row, decided on the *sibling* argument (`citations` has always been Laravel's) rather than on the property in the abstract; and **`messages`/`provider_calls` unpartitioned**, which does **not** say `postgresql-patterns` is wrong but that its precedent does not transfer — `audit_logs` is append-only with nothing holding a foreign key into it, `messages` is referenced. **ADR-073 is the one to read for the numbering hazard rather than for the analyzer**: it was decided in code, recorded in a docstring, and cited from five sites as *ADR-069*, a number this register had already assigned — so for a day a consequential decision had no ADR and its citations pointed at an unrelated one (`docs/22` § T41). A number is assigned here and nowhere else |

T65 also carries the fact that applies to every spec on every `ServerDataTable` route: **both layouts are in the DOM at once**, so a locator over a cell matches it twice. **Do not read which rows are open from this cell** (ADR-036) |
| [23-unverified-claims.md](23-unverified-claims.md) | Every `UNVERIFIED` marker in the skill library, triaged by how it closes, plus the claims raised by scaffolding, by ADR-030, by ADR-031…035, by the stub-completion effort and by the 2026-08-12 rulings that carry no marker — including the four things this host structurally cannot verify (the Actions runtime, and any mobile behaviour on a device), one real degradation that currently reaches the index as silence (a page classified as a picture loses its text with no warning), and the two auth claims that belong to Playwright rather than to Vitest — back-button-after-logout, and the org switch mid-flight — plus the manual end-to-end pass that would have closed both and has never been run, and the three raised by the shutdown-determinism effort — the daemon-restart revival ADR-044 acts on was never reproduced (only the crash-loop arm it *refutes* was measured), the two new `compose-invariants` checks have run only by hand on this host, and the extra invitations-list read has no known cause after six mechanisms were refuted — and the one raised by the live-parse effort, which is narrower than it looks: the live-parse **tests** are verified (they passed twice, and the skip guard was proven by hiding a fixture), while the **CI step** that runs them is unrun, since it depends on a ~3.5 GB image being exported to a runner's daemon — the same section also records two `-W default:` narrowings moving from *documented as measured* to *exercised by a real parse* — and the five raised by the bots-schema effort, two of which mislead in the same direction because something ran, reported success, and was **not the thing named**: PostgreSQL here is 16 while the project pins 18 (no construct was downgraded, but the index comments reason about a PG 18 planner behaviour 16 does not have), and the Playwright browser build the lockfile pins is a directory of symlinks into the build that is actually installed; plus no accessibility verification of any kind being possible on a host with no browser and no person, an unmet `ext-bcmath` waived at install, and the standing no-Docker gap, restated because the PG-version row depends on it — and a closing section that adds **no new rows on purpose**, re-running all five commands at the end of Phase B and widening their *scope* instead, because every screen the phase shipped inherits every one of them and the accessibility row's sharpest half is untestable by construction rather than merely unrun: the component suite loads no CSS, so which layout is visible at which width is asserted nowhere at all — and a closing section for **Phase C** that re-checks the same rows against three more screens and adds **one that is new in kind**: the Laravel↔FastAPI ingestion seam has no far side at all (`app/contracts/internal/` is empty and the router does not exist), so the deadline fix, the absent `X-KB-Bot-Id`, the internal body's shape and the two object-key prefixes are each verified only against themselves — a limitation no browser, database or daemon on this host would close — and a section for the adapter and RAG-stage effort that is the first in this file whose markers live in `services/` rather than in the skill library, and which exists to keep a **measurement** from being recorded as a **decision**: `chunker.MAX_TOKENS` is 700, the two pinned NVIDIA NIM ranking ids were pinned as a family without either pair window being read, and if either is 512 then reranking was scoring a truncated prefix of every full-size chunk. The shipped guard refuses loudly and errs toward a false refusal, so the risk today is a visible refusal and the risk of relaxing the guard is silence — one page-read of each model's catalog page discharges the question **and** the five `UNVERIFIED` ranking constants beside it, which is why the two rows close together or not at all |

## Where the invariants live

The rules most likely to be violated by a well-meaning implementation, and their source:

| Invariant | Source |
|---|---|
| Every tenant record carries an org identifier; every Qdrant point carries tenant + bot payload | `02` §8.2 |
| Every vector query filters org, bot access, active source status, active version | `07` §12.6 |
| Browser/mobile clients never call FastAPI directly — always through Laravel | `06` §11.1 |
| PostgreSQL is source of truth; Qdrant is a derived, rebuildable index | `06` §10.3, `19` ADR-010 |
| A source version stays searchable until its replacement is fully indexed and activated | `03` §8.9, `08` §13.5 |
| Deletion targets stable identifiers, never text matching, and is verified afterwards | `03` §8.17 |
| Retrieved source content is untrusted data and can never override instructions | `07` §12.14, `13` §18.6 |
| Citations derive from retrieved evidence, not free-form model output | `07` §12.16–12.17 |
| No provider credential ever reaches a client | `13` §18.2, `04` §8.20 |
| Both planes render an unhandled internal exception identically — 500, `internal_dependency`, `retryable: false` — **and every hop that copies that envelope preserves it**, so a relay reads `retryable` and the `errors` map rather than a subset | `19` ADR-029 + ADR-052 |
| No embedding or reranking model runs locally; both go through the provider adapter layer, and **reranking is an optional, capability-gated stage** whose skip is recorded on the trace | `19` ADR-030, `22` § C1 |
| One rule decides which connection embeds, and eligible connections that disagree on `(provider, model)` are refused rather than tie-broken — that pair *is* the vector space | `19` ADR-031 |
| Sparse retrieval is locally computed BM25; **no corpus statistic is ever stored in Qdrant**, and IDF is applied to the query vector from `(org_id, allowed_version_ids)` | `19` ADR-032 |
| The data plane's PostgreSQL write allow-list is `ALLOWED_TABLES` in `app/db/writes.py`; membership is *derived and rebuildable*, *untouched by any public API path*, *migrated by Laravel* — never a count | `19` ADR-012 + ADR-033 |
| An embedding space names its collection; the drift digest never does, and changing the embedding model or the sparse analyzer is a reindex | `19` ADR-034, ADR-035 |
| A count a legitimate change could make wrong, and that a reader would act on *as the rule*, is written as a rule or as the command that re-measures it — never as a number. Orientation counts stay, provided the sentence names where the authoritative list lives | `19` ADR-036, `22` § R1–R8 + G1 |
| Which of the two committed credential files fails **open** is measured, never reasoned: `seaweedfs` exits 255 without its identities file, `valkey` starts wide open without its ACL file — the reverse of what eight files said — and a `ping \| grep -q PONG` probe reports healthy against a wide-open server | `19` ADR-037 |
| The admin surface has **exactly one** credential — the Sanctum SPA cookie session. A bearer header on `api/*` is a 401 by definition; nothing mints a token, `HasApiTokens` is absent from `User`, and ability middleware is never a gate | `19` ADR-038 |
| An emailed capability is an opaque hashed database row, never a signed URL, and **never a path segment** | `19` ADR-039 |
| On the admin auth surface the N ways of failing one endpoint are **one response**, compared pairwise against each other. This is **not** the 403-admin/404-public deny-oracle property, whose reference is always a live control on a public surface — conflating the two produces a test that passes while asserting the wrong thing | `19` ADR-040, `13` §18.3 |
| An audit write failure **aborts** a state change and is **logged** for a session act, and which one applies is declared per operation in one constant — never chosen at the call site. Every ABORT-policy write sits in the same transaction as the change it records | `19` ADR-041, `15` §20 |
| Registration is invitation-gated; **no HTTP route creates an organization**, and the bootstrap command refuses to run when one exists and never accepts a password | `19` ADR-042, `02` §8.1 |
| A model whose read path runs before any organization is known carries **no** `#[ScopedBy]`, because `OrganizationScope` fails closed — and the bypass alternative is barred because the CI grep cannot see its singular form | `19` ADR-043, `22` § H1 |
| In **development** nothing self-restarts and `make down` removes every profile's containers; `unless-stopped` is production-only and lives in the base file. Both directions are gated, because Compose merges `restart:` by replacement and an unnamed service silently keeps the production policy | `19` ADR-044, `22` § I1 |
| A container's stop signal must be one **its own PID 1 handles** — an unhandled signal is discarded for PID 1, so a `stop_grace_period` without a handler buys delay rather than a drain. Set per service, never as one `STOPSIGNAL` for an image that runs more than one entrypoint | `19` ADR-045 |
| A pinned Docker subnet lives **outside** the daemon's dynamic address pools, or an unpinned network can be handed the pinned range; and the CIDR is named once, by the anchor that feeds both the network and `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `19` ADR-046, `22` § I5 |
| A provider credential is replaced only through its own endpoint, which re-authenticates the actor and carries its own limiter; the edit endpoint accepts no credential field, and a `revoked` or `invalid` connection **may** be rotated — the connection's own status is deliberately not check 5, and `kb-security-baseline` §18.4 now says so beside its own worked example | `19` ADR-047, `22` § J7 |
| The error envelope says whether its `message` was written for a person (`actionable`) — a client renders a server message only when that is true, and never infers an HTTP status from it | `19` ADR-053, `22` § J2 |
| A `capability_flags` entry is a **claim**: nothing verifies it on the write path, an incoherent embedding row surfaces in the readiness verdict's `rejected[]`, and an incoherent rerank row surfaces nowhere | `19` ADR-054, `22` § J1 |
| `key_version` names the **KEK** that wrapped the row and is written by `CredentialVault::seal()` alone; a credential rotation bumps `credential_version` and never `key_version`, or the row names a KEK that never wrapped it | `19` ADR-048, `13` §18.2 |
| An organization's designated embedding connection cannot be deleted: the composite `ON DELETE RESTRICT` is the authority and the 409 is only its message — undesignating first is a re-index decision, not a setting | `19` ADR-049, ADR-031 |
| A storage bound is strictly **wider** than the validation bound in front of it, so the boundary value is a 422 with a field to key on rather than a driver error rendered as a 500 | `19` ADR-050 |
| The provider capability vocabulary is `Capability` in the data plane; the control plane validates **spelling, not membership** (a pattern, never `Rule::in`), publishes no enum, and `packages/contracts` holds no copy | `19` ADR-051 |
| An ordered list of references to another tenant-owned table is a **table**, never a `jsonb` array — `jsonb` cannot carry a foreign key, so a chain stored that way leaves the primary model guarded by the database and its replacements guarded by whichever service last wrote them. A configuration snapshot may hold the chain; it is assembled from the source of truth and is not the source of truth | `19` ADR-055 |
| `bots.manage` is Owner and Admin (§6.3 as written); `bots.view` is held by **all four roles**, and that is an **extension of the specification** decided with the repo owner, not a reading of §6.4/§6.5, which never mention bots in either direction. The Analyst row is therefore no longer all-false | `19` ADR-056, `02` §6.3–6.5 |
| A stored evidence threshold is **nullable, has no default, and carries its scale**. The scale is a property of `(provider, model)`; `0.30` is a valid float on every scale, so a default would move only the refusal rate, only in aggregate, for one tenant, and fail no test. `uncalibrated` is not a scale and never reaches the column | `19` ADR-057, ADR-030 |
| The two-organization canary fixture is `tenantPair()` and nothing else; the canary is **moved** when indexed source content lands, never duplicated, and no property on it is typed `object` — `$t->botA` and `$t->botB` must not be interchangeable | `19` ADR-058, `22` § H9 |
| A paginated list is `{"data": {"<key>": [...], "meta": {...}}}` with one shared `meta` component, no generated links, 1-based pages, a closed sortable-column set per endpoint, and the **applied** query echoed rather than the requested one | `19` ADR-059 |
| Where a response body varies by caller, **the body says how it varied**. A client never re-derives a projection from a role or a permission: the role answers a question about the *session*, the projection is resolved *per record, per request*, and the two are allowed to disagree by one round trip | `19` ADR-060, ADR-056 |
| A field the server withheld is **omitted** from client form state, never seeded as `null` — `sometimes` leaves an absent key alone while a present `null` clears the column — and the control is not rendered at all, because a registered input submits its DOM value whether or not `defaultValues` named it | `19` ADR-061, `22` § M3 |
| The active-version pointer is `source_items.current_version_id` and there is **no second pointer** — `knowledge_sources` carries none, a single-file upload is a one-item source, and the data plane never assigns it. Two pointers nothing forces to agree is a lifecycle bug with no constraint to catch it | `19` ADR-062, `11` §16.4 |
| A version row carries `parser_cfg_version`, `ocr_cfg_version`, `chunker_cfg_version` and `embedding_model_version` spelled as the ingest key's own components, plus `activated_at` **and** `retired_at` — the two terms of the partial unique index that makes *at most one live version per item* provable by the database. One `published_at` cannot express the second term | `19` ADR-063, `22` § _Spec defects_ 1 |
| `knowledge_sources`, `source_items` and `source_versions` share **one** status vocabulary — `SourceState` in `app/ingestion/states.py`, as a `CHECK` and never a PG enum. The source-level rollup is computed for display, never a second column; the Qdrant `source_status` filter term is a copy of it, and a copy has no default. **There are four definitions of that vocabulary, not three** — the control-plane enum, the SQL CHECKs, the data-plane `StrEnum`, and `ACTIVE_SOURCE_STATUSES` in `app/retrieval/tenancy.py`, which is bare literals and is what the payload filter actually matches on; `tests/Contract/SourceStateParityTest.php` is the only thing joining them, and a divergence in the fourth is a **silent retrieval change** rather than a save-time error | `19` ADR-064, `22` § _Spec defects_ 4, § P3 |
| `content_hash` is `char(64) COLLATE "C"` hex on every table that holds one, with a format `CHECK`. This **overrules** `postgresql-patterns`' `bytea` line, which is owed a correction from that skill's owner and is wrong in writing until it lands | `19` ADR-065, `22` § P1 |
| `original/` is **source-scoped and a sibling of `versions/`**; `derived/` stays version-scoped. One object therefore serves every version, so `purge_retired_version` must never pass `include_original` — and retained-versus-missed is decided by the **disposition recorded before the sweep**, never by what enumeration finds. Overrules `seaweedfs-s3` NN1 and `kb-tenancy-isolation`:97, both owed a correction | `19` ADR-066, `22` § Q11 |
| A knowledge source is **organization-owned**; `X-KB-Bot-Id` is absent on ingestion and embedding readiness, and bot access is a **query-time** payload filter, never an index-time scope. The header set is inside the canonical string, so neither side can be corrected alone. Overrules `kb-internal-api-contracts`:64 | `19` ADR-067, `22` § Q13 |
| The **ingest key** (`identity.py`'s `INGEST_KEY_PARTS`, holding every `*_cfg_version`) and the **transport idempotency key** (`IngestionSubmission::fingerprint()`, holding none of them) are two different keys with two different jobs. `docs/08` §13.3 describes the first and is cited for the second; following it literally makes an OCR retune a silent no-op | `19` ADR-068, `08` §13.3, `22` § _Spec defects_ 1–2 |
| A rule whose only enforcement is a sentence is written down **as** a rule with no mechanism, never as an invariant. Both examples this row was written for **gained mechanisms on 2026-08-25, and closing them cost two live defects** (§ S1, § S2) — so read what each mechanism actually covers rather than the rule it is named after: `assert_writable` plus `test_write_allow_list_scan.py` catch *writing against a name that was never admitted* and nothing catches *admitting a wrong name*, and the active-version tripwire is narrower than the rule on purpose, because it is the part a scanner can decide. **The class of rule the row is about is not retired**, and § T40 is its newest instance in the place with the least cover of all: nothing watches `CLAUDE.md`'s claims about code | `22` § Q5, § Q6, § S1, § S2, § T40 |
| The **BM25 analyzer** is one function analyzing both passages and queries — NFKC → casefold → NFKC, character bigrams for scripts written without word separators, maximal word-character runs elsewhere (combining marks included), punctuation separating. It is inside the collection name (ADR-034), so a change to it, or to any of the three BM25 constants, the term-id modulus or the hash personalization, **re-embeds the dense vectors at a provider's per-token price**. `bm25/v1` is cheap to change **only while no corpus has ever been indexed**, and that is an expiry rather than a revisit trigger | `19` ADR-073, ADR-032, ADR-034 |
| `retrieval_traces` is **Laravel's**, written by the relay finalizer in the same transaction as the message, the citations and the usage row. It is not on the data plane's write allow-list, for the same reason `citations` never was: an admin screen reads it, and ADR-033's property 2 is the one that bites. Consequence to carry — `erase_data_subject` now sweeps **two** of its three verbatim columns over the core-api seam, and only `evaluation_results.retrieved_evidence` is a local statement | `19` ADR-074, ADR-033, `22` § T28 |
| `messages` and `provider_calls` are **not partitioned**, and retention is `retention_expires_at` plus a partial index on `conversations`. `postgresql-patterns` is not wrong; its precedent does not transfer — `audit_logs` is append-only with nothing holding a foreign key into it, while `messages` is referenced, so partitioning trades referential-integrity constraints for a retention mechanism the schema already has. The ruling re-opens on a **measurement** — a retention sweep's p99 outgrowing its batch window, or the partial index no longer being chosen — never on a feeling, and the migration that reverses it is a full-table rewrite budgeted as one | `19` ADR-075, ADR-041, `22` § Q3, § T23 |
